AND project_id = ?\",\n            (camp_id, project_id),\n        ).fetchone()\n        if row is None:\n            return None\n        if row[\"status\"] != \"active\":\n            return False\n\n        new_completed = min(row[\"days_completed\"] + days, row[\"days_required\"])\n        status = \"complete\" if new_completed >= row[\"days_required\"] else \"active\"\n        conn.execute(\n            \"UPDATE crafting_projects SET days_completed = ?, status = ? \"\n            \"WHERE campaign_id = ? AND project_id = ?\",\n            (new_completed, status, camp_id, project_id),\n        )\n\n        if status == \"complete\":\n            conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO campaign_inventory (campaign_id, item_slug, quantity, owner, source) \"\n                \"VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'crafting') \"\n                \"ON CONFLICT(campaign_id, item_slug, owner) \"\n                \"DO UPDATE SET quantity = quantity + excluded.quantity\",\n                (camp_id, row[\"item_slug\"], 1, row[\"character_id\"]),\n            )\n        conn.commit()\n\n    return {\"id\": project_id, \"days_completed\": new_completed, \"status\": status}\n\n\n# --- Session scheduling ---\n\n\ndef create_session(camp_id, session_id, starts_at, duration_minutes, agenda):\n    \"\"\"Create a scheduled session for a campaign.\n\n    Returns the saved session on success, None if the campaign is missing,\n    or False if the session id already exists in the campaign.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM campaigns WHERE id = ?\", (camp_id,)).fetchone() is None:\n            return None\n        if conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT 1 FROM sessions WHERE campaign_id = ? AND id = ?\",\n            (camp_id, session_id),\n        ).fetchone() is None:\n            return None\n\n        all_char_ids = set(present) | set(absent)\n        if all_char_ids:\n            placeholders = \",\".join(\"?\" * len(all_char_ids))\n            rows = conn.execute(\n                \"SELECT id FROM campaign_characters WHERE campaign_id = ?            (session_id,),\n        ).fetchone()\n        if row is None:\n            return None\n        combatants = _session_combatants(conn, session_id)\n        if not combatants:\n session is\n    missing, or False if the target is not a combatant in the session.\n    \"\"\"\n    with _get_db() as conn:\n        if conn.execute(\"SELECT 1 FROM combat_sessions WHERE id = ?\", AND target = ?\",\n            (session_id, active[\"name\"]),\n        )\n        conn.execute(\n            \"DELETE FROM conditions WHERE session_id = ? AND target = ? ORDER BY id\",\n            (session_id,),\n        ).fetchall()\n        for r in rows:\n            conditions.setdefault(r[\"target\"], []).append(\n                {\"condition\": r[\"condition\"], \"remaining_rounds\": r[\"remaining_rounds\"]}\n            )\n\n        return {\n            \"id\": session_id,\n            \"round\": round_num,\n            \"turn_index\": turn_index,\n            \"active\": {\"name\": active[\"name\"], \"score\": active[\"score\"]},\n            \"conditions\": conditions,\n        }\n\n\n# --- Compendium ---\n\n\ndef create_monster(slug, name, cr, armor_class, hit_points, tags):\n    \"\"\"Create a monster entry; D&D DM Tools API — Codebase Guide\n\nThis is a small Flask REST API for D&D 5e DM utilities. It is intentionally\nstateless in memory between requests; all durable state lives in a local SQLite\ndatabase.\n\nThis document describes the implementation **after** the refactoring\ncheckpoint, not a future design.\n\n## Quick start\n\n```bash\nPORT=8000 ./run.sh\n```\n\nVerify the server is up:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health\n```\n\nCheck the storage layer:\n\n```bash\ncurl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/storage/status\n```\n\n`run.sh` bootstraps the vendored dependencies in `./.deps` if they are missing\nand starts the Flask development server in the foreground on `127.0.0.1` using\nthe `PORT` environment variable.\n\n## Runtime and framework versions\n\n- Python 3.14.6\n- Flask 3.1.3\n\nPinned in `requirements.txt` and `VERSION-PINS.json`.\n\n## Entry point and module layout\n\n| File | Responsibility |\n| ---- | -------------- |\n| `app.py` | Creates the Flask application, registers the `routes` blueprint, and runs the server. Calls `storage.reset_db()` on startup so every server process begins with a clean, initialized database. |\n| `routes.py` | All HTTP route handlers. Validates input, delegates to domain/services/storage, and shapes JSON responses. Common response and access-control patterns are factored into small helpers. |\n| `domain.py` | Pure, side-effect-free D&D 5e math and static tables (XP, modifiers, dice, rests, initiative, etc.). |\n| `services.py` | Higher-level workflows that combine domain logic with storage (e.g., encounter builder, analytics). |\n| `storage.py` | SQLite persistence layer. All SQL lives here; routes never touch the database directly. Includes idempotent schema migrations for columns added across checkpoints. |\n| `run.sh` | Bootstrap and server start script. |\n| `requirements.txt` | Flask dependency pin. |\n| `VERSION-PINS.json` | Shared version metadata for the benchmark harness. |\n| `game.db` | SQLite database file created automatically next to `app.py`. |\n\n## State, persistence, and routing\n\n### Persistence\n\n- Storage is provided by SQLite in `game.db`.\n- The schema version is `1` and is hard-coded in `storage.py`.\n- `storage.init_db()` creates tables and back-fills any columns added since the\n  initial schema; `storage.reset_db()` drops and recreates all tables (used by\n  `POST /v1/storage/reset` and by `app.py` on startup).\n- All tables use string primary keys for domain entities (campaigns, combat\n  sessions, users, compendium entries). Junction tables enforce composite keys.\n- Foreign keys are declared in the DDL but are not enabled at runtime; the\n  application enforces referential integrity through the storage layer.\n\n### Request routing\n\nRoutes are grouped in a Flask Blueprint (`api`) and registered in `app.py`.\nThe route layer does three things:\n\n1. Parse and validate the JSON body.\n2. Call the appropriate domain function, service, or storage function.\n3. Return the same JSON body and status code as the previous checkpoint.\n\nRoutes do not contain SQL or business math beyond input validation. Repeated\npatterns—such as \"campaign must exist\" or \"only the owner may access\"—are\nfactored into helpers in `routes.py` so each endpoint reads as a short list of\ncontract checks.\n\n### Determinism\n\n- No randomness is used in responses.\n- Initiative order, combat turn order, and condition decay are deterministic.\n- Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2; the token returned on login is deterministic\n  (`session-{username}`).\n\n## Main API groups\n\n### Core utilities\n\n- `GET /health` — liveness check.\n- `POST /v1/dice/stats` — statistics for expressions like `2d6+3`.\n- `POST /v1/checks/ability` — d20 ability check result.\n- `POST /v1/encounters/adjusted-xp` — encounter difficulty for level-3 parties.\n- `POST /v1/initiative/order` — deterministic initiative ordering.\n\n### Combat\n\n- `POST /v1/combat/sessions` — create a session and store combatants.\n- `POST /v1/combat/sessions/<id>/conditions` — attach a condition to a combatant.\n- `POST /v1/combat/sessions/<id>/advance` — advance the turn and decay conditions.\n\n### Characters\n\n- `POST /v1/characters/ability-modifier`\n- `POST /v1/characters/proficiency`\n- `POST /v1/characters/derived-stats`\n\n### Auth\n\n- `POST /v1/auth/register` — create a user with role `dm` or `player`.\n- `POST /v1/auth/login` — validate credentials and return a deterministic
